is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. gambiae and An. coluzzii) as stated in the title and abstract.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (Kdr L1014F) and Ace-1 G280S (Ace-1R G119S) as described in the Methods section (page 4) and results tables (Tables 1, 2, and 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 1, 2, and 3 provide detailed genotype counts (SS, RS, RR) and allele frequencies for both markers across different species and study arms.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in 40 villages around Bouaké, Côte d'Ivoire, as described in the Methods section (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field data collected during a cluster-randomized controlled trial.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies the location as 40 villages around the district of Bouaké, Côte d'Ivoire (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection period is clearly stated as May 2017 to April 2019 (page 2, 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: While the study is part of a larger trial (Sternberg et al. 2018, 2021), this specific paper reports original molecular data on insecticide resistance markers and Plasmodium infection status not previously published in the cited trial papers.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and statistical results are provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the association between insecticide resistance markers (Kdr L1014F and Ace-1R G119S) and Plasmodium infection status in wild Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii populations in Bouaké, Côte d'Ivoire. Genotyping was performed on 1,255 mosquitoes collected between 2017 and 2019. The results showed no significant association between the resistance markers and Plasmodium infection status.
